sentences.text: THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT Heard Sri.B.Mahesh, learned counsel who argued on behalf of Sri.Hanumanthappa A., learned counsel on record for the appellant.
Also heard Sri.O.Mahesh, learned counsel on record for respondent No.3 who appeared through Video Conference and Sri.D.Vijay Kumar, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.5.

The present appeal is filed questioning the quantum awarded as compensation in favour of the appellant by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Harapanahalli, through orders in MVC No.76/2012 dated 30.12.2015.
A sum of Rs.2,26,400/- was awarded as compensation by the Claims Tribunal fixing joint and several liability upon the respondents.
On this day, learned counsel for the appellant made a proposal for enhancement of compensation by Rs.1,20,000/-.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for respondent No.3 and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.5 though made their submissions with regard to the merits of the matter, however, a perusal of the record goes to show that the proposal mooted is justifiable.

Finally, both the learned counsels i.e.
learned counsel for respondent No.3 and learned counsel for respondent No.5 agreed for the said proposal.
However, requested the Court to pass the order that the enhanced amount carry no interest.
The learned counsel for the appellant agreed for the same.
4. On perusal of the record it is found that the Tribunal has awarded very meager amount under the head pain and NC: 2023:KHC:45605 sufferings and loss of amenities in life.
Also considering the nature of injuries sustained, it can be safely presumed that the appellant would not have attended his normal pursuits for a longer period.
Also for calculating loss of future earnings, notional income taken is also on lower side.
Further, no amount is awarded as compensation for loss of earning during laid up period.
Therefore, in all, the request of the learned counsel for the appellant seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.1,20,000/- appears justifiable.
5. Thus, the appeal is disposed of by enhancing the amount of compensation to an extent of Rs.1,20,000/-.
However, the enhanced amount carries no interest.
On deposit, the entire amount be released in favour of the appellant.
